name: Time-Lapse Kymograph Generation
description:
You are a biophysicist studying cell division kinetics. Your goal is to generate a kymograph (space-time plot) from a 5D hyperstack to visualize chromosome movement over time.

1. Open the built-in sample 'Mitosis (26MB, 5D stack)' via File > Open Samples > Mitosis.
   - This is a 5D image: X, Y, Z (5 slices), Channels (2), Time (51 frames).

2. Prepare the image:
   - Split the channels (Image > Color > Split Channels). Keep the Red channel (chromosomes) and close the Green channel.
   - The Red channel is still a 4D stack (XYZT). You need to project the Z-dimension while keeping Time.
   - Perform a Z-Projection (Image > Stacks > Z Project...): Use 'Max Intensity' projection. CRITICAL: Ensure 'All time frames' is checked so you get a Time-series result (XYT), not just a single image.
   - Save this intermediate time-lapse stack to ~/ImageJ_Data/results/mitosis_projection.tif

3. Generate the Kymograph:
   - Select the 'Straight Line' tool.
   - Draw a line through the center of the dividing cell, crossing both sets of chromosomes along the axis of division.
   - Perform a Reslice (Image > Stacks > Reslice...) to generate the kymograph. Use default settings (Output spacing: 1.0 pixel, Start at: Top/Left).
   - Note: A kymograph exchanges spatial position (X along line) with Time (Y axis). The resulting image height should correspond to the number of time points.
   - Save the final kymograph image to ~/ImageJ_Data/results/mitosis_kymograph.tif
